claims.text: A decoupled multiscale approach will model lattice and electronic thermal transport separately in HfNbTaTiZr.
The decoupled approach will predict HfNbTaTiZr thermal conductivity more accurately than earlier combined approaches.
The intended initial material is high-purity, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr bulk crystal.
One modeled sample set will reproduce a condition containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
A second sample set will contain minimal extrinsic impurities for tests below 200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr may be comparable.
The separate treatment of interatomic force constants and electronic band parameters underpins enhanced predictive accuracy.
Interatomic force constants govern the modeled phonon transport.
Electronic band parameters influence electron scattering and electronic heat transport.
Avoiding a single Debye temperature and conflated analytical approximations reduces errors caused by oversimplified models.
Ab initio force constants and DFT-derived electronic structures improve the physical fidelity of the separate transport channels.
Improved channel-level physical fidelity leads to more reliable total thermal-conductivity predictions.
Prediction error will improve by approximately 15–20% relative to previous models.
Earlier methods that conflated lattice and electronic contributions typically deviate from experiment by more than ±20%.
Oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr specimens have measured total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K·m) at high temperatures.
The model is expected to be primarily valid for well-characterized, nearly defect-free HfNbTaTiZr from 300 to 1200 K.
Accuracy below 200 K is less certain when additional scattering mechanisms or defect states are significant.
Oxygen impurities and unforeseen defect states may limit the decoupled model's ability to account for complex scattering interactions.
The hypothesis is falsified if prediction error is not improved by at least 15–20% relative to earlier models.
The hypothesis is also falsified if independent measurements do not support the predicted separation of lattice and electronic contributions within the stated error margins.

contradictions.description: The samples are described as defect-free or nearly defect-free while one required specimen contains 1 wt.% oxygen, a substantial extrinsic impurity condition that is also acknowledged as a possible source of defect states and scattering.
